title: dotnet_check envelope

$janet.$comment: Not JSON Schema. Read by scripts/Test-OutputContracts.ps1.

description: A tagged union. 'status' is the discriminator and the only field both arms share besides contract and target, because a caller that has not read the discriminator has no business reading anything else.

succeeded.description: Exactly one thing: the build succeeded AND every test passed. Mirrors the exit code.

errors.description: Every instance, verbatim and never truncated. An error is the payload.

warnings.description: Grouped by code. Collapsed, never silently dropped.

omittedInstances.description: The honest truncation marker. Positive means the instance list was capped.

newWarnings.description: NULL MEANS NO COMPARISON HAPPENED -- no -New, or no prior baseline -- not 'none were new'. Otherwise every warning absent from the baseline, verbatim and uncapped, because a new warning is error-like.

resolvedWarningCount.description: Same nullability, same reading: null is 'not compared', not 'none resolved'.

comparedTo.description: The prior baseline's timestamp, or null on the first run for this target and configuration.

saved.description: Whether this run's census was written back. Only a successful build is: a failed build is a partial census.

tests.description: NULL MEANS NOT RUN -- -NoTests, or the build failed. Which one is visible from build.succeeded. It does not mean a suite with no tests.

succeeded.description: False when any test failed, when dotnet test exited non-zero, or when any assembly's results are partial. The counters alone cannot say this: a crashed test host reports fewer tests, not failed ones.

runnerExitCode.description: dotnet test's own exit code, propagated rather than recomputed. Non-zero with failed=0 is the signature of an aborted run.

abort.description: The runner's abort banner -- the exception that killed the test host and the top of its stack -- or null for a run that finished. The one channel that names why a host died; best effort, the exit code is the verdict. NOT set by an ordinary test failure: xUnit files its per-test '[FAIL]' line as a run-level RunInfo Error, which until contract 7 was handed back here as though it were a crash.

durationSeconds.description: WALL CLOCK for the whole run, earliest start to latest finish across every assembly. What you waited. Diagnostic, never a budget: nothing fails for being slow, and suite duration is machine-dependent.

testTimeSeconds.description: Every test's own duration added up. EXCEEDS durationSeconds whenever collections ran in parallel, so this and durationSeconds are different questions and neither is 'the' duration: this one is where the time went. Measured on JanetHome 2026-09-07: 17.07s of test time inside 3.96s of clock.

message.description: Verbatim and whole. It is the payload, and read from the TRX rather than scraped from the console.

status.description: 'aborted' is a crashed run's leftovers and FAILS the run: its counters are what the host lived to write, not a result. 'empty' ran nothing and does NOT fail the run -- a filter matching nothing in an assembly writes a TRX with no definitions and zero counters, which is the same shape a half-written crash file has. They are told apart by whether the runner closed the file out (ResultSummary outcome Completed/Failed) and by whether a run-level RunInfo Error actually reads as an abort banner. Absence of a name or of counters is NOT evidence of a crash; treating it as such reported a narrow filter over six assemblies as five crashes.

durationSeconds.description: Wall clock for this assembly, from the TRX's own Times. Falls back to testTimeSeconds when the file carries no Times.

testTimeSeconds.description: This assembly's per-test durations added up. Zero for an assembly that reported no results.

resultsFile.description: The TRX this row was read from, kept on disk rather than deleted with the run. Open it instead of re-running the suite to see something the envelope did not carry.

slowest.description: The slowest test CLASSES by summed test time, longest first, at most five. The class is the unit reported because it is the unit that serialises: xUnit runs collections in parallel and defaults to one collection per class, so a slow class costs its full time however many cores are idle. Empty when no TRX carried durations. Diagnostic output, not a budget.

resultsDirectory.description: Where this run's TRX files are. They now OUTLIVE the call: they used to be deleted in a finally, which made the envelope the only account of a run that ever existed and left a session re-running the whole suite with its own logger to learn anything it had not thought to include. A bounded number of recent run directories is kept.

graph.description: NULL MEANS NOT APPLICABLE -- this repository carries no graph convention: no .graph directory or scripts\graph.ps1, and no razorgraph server declared in its .mcp.json. Most repositories carry neither. It does not mean a graph is missing; that is status 'absent'.

via.description: Which convention answered (contract 6). 'script': a .graph directory refreshed by scripts\graph.ps1. 'razorgraph': a graph held by the RazorGraph MCP server the repository's .mcp.json declares, matched by the solution or project it was built from lying under this repository, and rebuilt in place with build_solution or build_graph.

graphId.description: The server-side id of the graph. razorgraph only; null for the script convention and for an absent graph.

path.description: The graph file (script), or the solution or project the server graphed (razorgraph).

canRefresh.description: False with status 'stale' means the repo has a graph and no way to rebuild it here. Staleness is reported even where it cannot be fixed. Under razorgraph, false with 'absent' means the server holds no graph of this repository or did not answer: nothing is built that nobody asked for, so build one with build_solution when you want it.

handle.description: Pass this back to the same tool to poll. A full rebuild can outlast a client's call timeout, and a slow build presenting as a dead tool is the failure this arm exists to prevent.

line.description: Null for a diagnostic MSBuild reported against a file rather than a position.
